title: 10 Parachutes, 1 Big Bang: ISRO's Gaganyaan Test #Shorts
description:
ISRO Gaganyaan crew module service module separation test, Thiruvananthapuram, ISRO news, space milestones.
Before a crew capsule can come home, it has to let go of its service module. On 16 October 2026, ISRO announced it had completed ground tests of this step: power and fluid lines were severed, pyrotechnics fired, and the two modules were pushed apart, while the avionics, navigation and heat shield came through the shock. Nothing flew. After almost six years of "safety first", uncrewed G1 and its passenger, the half-humanoid robot Vyommitra, are one step closer.
Bang or parachutes? Tell us your favourite part and your city!
Subscribe for more hopeful science.
Visuals: labelled 2D illustration, not real footage.
Source: ISRO announcement, 16 Oct 2026 (VSSC ground tests)
#Shorts #Space #Science #Futuretech #Astronomy

OWNER NOTE - SCHEDULING: Hold rule says no new Shorts before the 7-day numbers (about 1 Nov). This Short is evergreen until G1 launches, so publish on or after 1 Nov, unless ISRO announces a G1 date first (then publish sooner and update the G1 lines).

SERIES: Space Milestones. FORMAT: vertical 9:16, about 50s.
Alt titles: "0 Flights, 1 Big Test: Gaganyaan Splits Apart #Shorts"; "1 Split Test: ISRO's Gaganyaan Modules Part Ways #Shorts"

CAST: Arjun is the only narrator, voice-only, calm, no hype. Lumen appears once in a silent 2s stock reaction cutaway. Vyommitra appears only as a name card (no ISRO still unless licence confirmed).

SCRIPT (VO):
0:00-0:03 "Before it comes home, India's Gaganyaan capsule must cut loose from its power module." Text: THE GOODBYE TEST / ISRO Gaganyaan crew module separation
0:03-0:10 "On 16 October, ISRO announced it had completed a series of crew module and service module separation tests at VSSC, Thiruvananthapuram. Ground tests. Nothing flew." Text: Announced 16 Oct 2026 · VSSC / GROUND TESTS. NOTHING FLEW.
0:10-0:16 "In orbit, the two fly as one. The service module supplies power and propulsion, then is discarded before re-entry." Text: Orbit → Separation → Re-entry
0:16-0:18 Lumen, silent reaction
0:18-0:27 "How do you part them? The lines are severed, pyrotechnics fire, and the modules are pushed apart. A sharp shock. ISRO says the tests confirmed the design." Text: Lines severed · Modules pushed apart / Design confirmed
0:27-0:33 "The capsule's avionics, inertial navigation and heat-shield protection survived it, and so did the pyrotechnics tied to its uprighting system." Text: Avionics ✓ Navigation ✓ Heat shield ✓ Uprighting pyros ✓
0:33-0:38 "After re-entry, ten parachutes open in sequence: two, two, three, three. Those are tested separately." Text: 2 + 2 + 3 + 3 = 10 / Tested separately
0:38-0:43 "The uncrewed G1 flight is targeted for 2026. It was first planned for December 2020. Almost six years of safety first." Text: G1: targeted 2026 (as of 23 Oct 2026) / First planned: Dec 2020
0:43-0:50 "Would you trust the bang or the parachutes? Tell us below, and follow Space Milestones. G1's passenger? A half-humanoid robot, Vyommitra." Text: BANG or PARACHUTES? / Follow: Space Milestones / G1 passenger: Vyommitra

EDIT PLAN (Mr. Cut): 23 shots, a cut every 2-3s. One self-made flat 2D animation of two labelled shapes ("Crew Module", "Service Module") reused throughout, with "Illustration" always on screen. Any stock rocket clip tagged "Representative footage, not ISRO". Music: soft awe bed ducked to -18 dB, low impact at "Nothing flew", swell at 0:20, resolve at 0:43. Captions bold white, in safe zone. Credits strip: "Illustration: Hopeverse Media · Stock: Pixabay/NASA · Music: [track]".
Shots: 1 hook snap-apart flash; 2 title; 3 Thiruvananthapuram map pin; 4 test rig; 5 "NOTHING FLEW" stamp; 6-8 orbit timeline, amber glow on service module, service module discarded; 9 Lumen; 10-13 lines snap, pyro flash, modules drift apart, shock ripple; 14-16 checklist ticks; 17-18 descent and four groups of parachutes; 19-20 calendar 2020 to 2026; 21 silhouette with "?"; 22 follow card; 23 Vyommitra name card and credits, fade.

PINNED COMMENT: "Bang or parachutes? Vote below and tell us your city 👇"

THUMBNAIL: Own flat 2D artwork (no ISRO photo): capsule and boxy service module splitting apart, saffron spark between, faint row of parachutes. Text "BANG OR PARACHUTES?" Deep navy background, saffron-orange text, white outlines. Backup: two modules with bright gap and "GROUND TEST" tag, text "SPLIT TEST DONE".
